video_title: ASÍ ES CUBRIR A UN EQUIPO NBA DESDE DENTRO

quotes.speaker: Sam Merrill
quotes.summary_phrase: Sam Merrill on developing a quicker release for the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I've definitely worked on since I've been in the NBA on having a slightly quicker release.

text_blocks.speaker: Nacho Losilla
text_blocks.text: Hi Sam, I really knew you were a shooter before watching you there, but I was really impressed watching your shooting form here with that move that you make in the middle. How do you build up your mechanic? Because it was amazing watching it, a very, very quick release. Was it something you made naturally, that middle move on the shooting, or was it something you built up your mechanic? How do you develop the shot?

text_blocks.speaker: Sam Merrill
text_blocks.text: Yeah, I would say my form has always been pretty natural. Just growing up playing, that's kind of how it formed for me. But I've definitely worked on since I've been in the NBA on having a slightly quicker release. And that's just from doing a lot of drills, doing drills where I have a defender that I got to get it off before he can block it or what not. So a lot of reps and experience and it's gotten quicker and I'm comfortable about it.

quotes.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell on trade rumors and his commitment to the Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: At the end of the day, it's not my choice about where I want to go.

text_blocks.speaker: Nacho Losilla
text_blocks.text: I have one last curiosity I would like to know, because you've been, of course, the potential Lakers move are always one of the most trending things on social media and stuff like that. And until the Walker trade, you were one of the main names to the center, to the new Luka Doncic center guy. I don't know if you are, because there are players who look at these things more, there are players who are like, I don't care about all this. How do you live or how do you react to all this news about you potentially becoming the new Lakers center?

text_blocks.speaker: Donovan Mitchell
text_blocks.text: You just hear about it, you understand that it's a possibility and you just have to live with it. At the end of the day, it's not my choice about where I want to go. It's not my choice about a lot of the things I do in my job. I just have to go out there and be the best player I can be and in the summer I have to focus on improving even more. So I hear the noise, I listen to it, I understand it, but I don't let it impact my life on or off the court.

quotes.speaker: Jarrett Allen
quotes.summary_phrase: Jarrett Allen on defensive focus and team synergy with Evan Mobley
quotes.excerpt: We have conversations every day, training camp, and on like how we're going to keep that going.

text_blocks.speaker: Nacho Losilla
text_blocks.text: You are one of the best duos of big men in the NBA. Are you looking into some specific details or some stuff to like try to be even better or have even better impact on the playoffs as a duo? Which things do you look at? You and Jarrett Allen, yeah, because I asked Jarrett about your duo as one of the best pairs of big men in the NBA. So how do you look into details? What do you try to look like, we have to do this better, we have to communicate in this one better? Which details do you put your attention?

text_blocks.speaker: Jarrett Allen
text_blocks.text: With me and him, it's just about being on the same page. Whenever we're on the same page, we're, like you said, one of the best duels in the game. So we have conversations every day, training camp, and on like how we're going to keep that going and keep that synergy going to where we're always on the same page. I know where he's at on the court and he knows where I'm at on the court and we can just bounce off each other. So that's really our main focus with that duo. Right now we have a little bit of a different team and different dynamic and I think a lot of it right now we're focusing on is defense and making that our main focus right now and making sure our defense is top five in the league and then from there our offense is going to carry itself. So I think defensively was the focus.

quotes.speaker: Peyton Watson
quotes.summary_phrase: Peyton Watson on his role and learning from the playoffs
quotes.excerpt: Just take advantage of the minutes that I am receiving instead of thinking about what I'm not receiving.

text_blocks.speaker: Nacho Losilla
text_blocks.text: When you started in the league as a rookie, during half that playing time, last year you had a category role in the regular season. Now, in which parts or what did the playoffs teach you about what did you need to do to earn more minutes, to have a bigger playing time in the playoffs?

text_blocks.speaker: Peyton Watson
text_blocks.text: One, I mean, obviously don't limit mistakes. I think that's something, you know, obviously to get basketball we play, it's going to be mistakes all over the place, but trying to limit those and then try to just play my game, play with enough confidence. You know, obviously in the playoffs minutes go down, so just take advantage of those minutes and whatever I get. And once you take advantage, you do well in those minutes, you're going to keep getting minutes. So I think it's just take advantage of the minutes that I am receiving instead of thinking about what I'm not receiving.

quotes.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Craig Porter Jr. on the importance of defense for undrafted players
quotes.excerpt: The only way you're going to get on the court is defense.

text_blocks.speaker: Nacho Losilla
text_blocks.text: You coming to the league as an undrafted and having to earn your career and now building a role in a real contender, what did you learn like trying to survive in the NBA and having a role that can change from one game to other game in a drastic way, or to having a lot of minutes if some guys are out, to being on the bench? What have you learned in this journey?

text_blocks.speaker: Craig Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: I feel like, because I mean, again, when I came out of college and I was doing a lot of my pre-draft workouts, like coaches honestly, they told me straight up like, everybody in the NBA is getting looked at because they can't score or their offense. So the only way you're going to get on the court is defense. So I understood that a lot of the things that would get me on the court are the little things, hustling, playing defense and rebounding too. That's one of the things I'm good at at my size and just understanding that just plays a big role into it and it'll allow you to, honestly, pick your spots and you'll be able to do those little things while also getting a bigger role. So I feel like it's beneficial and you have to understand that, again, that's what will get you on the court, which is the main focus.
